neighbours.label: Verb of scholarly refinement or compilation applied to a prior work or idea (refined, expanded, codified, compiled, defined, developed, adapted), peaking on the verb right before its object
fire: In the decades after the war, the chemist Nadia Okafor later revised and expanded the original periodic tables her mentor had drawn up.
By the late 1800s, a Scottish schoolmaster had codified the rules of the sport, replacing the loose local customs that came before.
The linguist who first defined the notion of a phoneme was working from earlier sketches by his teacher, which he gradually refined into a theory.
Over many winters the folklorist compiled a collection of village songs and then adapted them for a children's choir.
Later economists developed the model Ricardo had outlined, extending it with new assumptions about trade and labour.
Her second edition thoroughly updated and expanded the textbook, adding chapters on genetics and field methods.
The engineer perfected the early design of the pump, and a student later refined the valve system for mass production.
Medieval scribes copied and glossed the treatise, and a monk in Padua adapted the commentary for use in the university lectures.
quiet: In the decades after the war, the chemist Nadia Okafor later burned the original periodic tables her mentor had drawn up.
By the late 1800s, a Scottish schoolmaster had abandoned the rules of the sport, preferring the loose local customs that came before.
The linguist who first met the young phonetician was working from a rented room in the city, where he gradually grew tired of the noise.
Over many winters the folklorist walked through the villages and then sang the songs for a children's choir.
Later economists criticised the model Ricardo had outlined, mocking it for its assumptions about trade and labour.
Her second edition was printed on cheap paper, with a new cover showing a field of wheat and a small tractor.
The engineer was fond of the early design of the pump, and a student later tripped over the valve system in the workshop.
Medieval scribes were fed in the abbey kitchen, and a monk in Padua carried the manuscript across the river to the university.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, random arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Strongest hits are verbs like refined/expanded/codified/compiled/defined/developed on an authorial act upon an earlier work, plus some 'of'/'the' after such verbs; the mix is wide and sparse (0.2% density), so coverage will probably be partial. Positive pole is a separate biography/history-title context.
